lots.title: Provision of Minor Disability Adaptations (Minor Building Works) in Privately Owned Properties
lots.description: Measured Term Contract for the installation of equipment and minor works at properties for people with disabilities. Scope covers the supply and installation of mobility/adaptation equipment (grab rails, ramps, thresholds, shower seats, stair rails, raised-height WCs, accessible doors, door aperture widening, accessible taps and electrical fittings, doorbells and keysafes) in clients' homes for the London Borough of Bexley, operating 1 November 2026 to 31 October 2028 with discretionary two one-year extensions. Works are ordered per-job via Council-issued Works Approval Forms and priced from an agreed pricing schedule; this document is the contract specification and is to be read with the Pricing Schedule under JCT MTC contract terms.
requirements: Contract period 1 November 2026 – 31 October 2028 with option for the Council to extend in one-year increments for up to two further years.

All work is commissioned per-job by a Council-issued Works Approval Form; work may not commence before the Form is issued and any variation must be agreed by or on behalf of the Authorised Officer before proceeding.

Response-time tiers: Code A (hospital discharge) within 24 hours of receipt, Code B (emergency) within 48 hours, Code C (urgent) within 5 working days, Code D (standard) within 15 working days; financial penalties of £100 per day may apply for Code A delays.
All works to be compliant with JCT MTC 2024 Terms and Conditions (including the above response-time tiers and penalty clause); JCT MTC 2016 also referenced for invoicing and VAT.

Contractor must submit an Application for Payment before invoicing; invoices must be submitted within six months of the Works Approval Form date and within the month following the invoice period, and payment will normally be made within 30 days of receipt and agreement.
Majority of works under this contract are VAT exempt; VAT must be shown separately as a strictly net extra charge when applicable.

All operatives who visit clients' homes must hold an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check; the Contractor must maintain a continually updated record of cleared staff and provide it to the Authorised Officer on request.
Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006 (TUPE) applies; staff of incumbent contractors may transfer to the successful bidder.

Contractor must comply with the Safety Schemes in Procurement (SSIP) Forum competence standards (e.g., CHAS, EXOR Health and Safety, or OHSAS 18001 registration) and maintain a compliant registration for the duration of the contract.

All operatives must wear visible photographic identification cards with employee name, trade, contractor name/address, contact number and expiry date (no more than 1 year from issue); cards must be produced on request.

Works must comply with current UK building regulations and relevant statutory undertakers' requirements; applications and consents to Building Control must be copied to the Authorised Officer before works commence.

All electrical works must be carried out in accordance with the BS 7671:2008 IET Wiring Regulations 18th Edition; a Part P-compliant electrical installation certificate must be provided on completion of any new circuit.
Gas-related works must comply with the Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 and be performed by Gas Safe-registered personnel.

Safety and toughened glazing must be clearly and permanently marked, in accordance with BS EN 12600, BS 952-1:1995 Parts 1 & 2 and BS 6262-4:2018, and comply with Approved Document K of the Building Regulations and Regulation 14 of the Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations 1992.
Personal protective equipment must conform to the Personal Protective Equipment at Work (Amendment) Regulations 2022; eye protection must be marked in conformity with BS EN ISO 16321 (2022).
Working at Height Regulations 2005 apply; safe working method statements and generic risk assessments are required before any work at height or hot works, and the Authorised Officer must be notified.

Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 (CDM 2015) apply where relevant; no additional costs for the Principal Contractor role will be paid as this is deemed included in the Pricing Schedule.

Contractor must comply with the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 (CAR 2012) and the Council's Asbestos Policy; no asbestos-containing materials may be used, and suspected asbestos must be reported immediately and not removed by the Contractor.

COSHH 2002 written assessments must be available on-site before hazardous substances are used; all waste must be disposed of under the Environmental Protection Act 1990 via a licensed carrier and Waste Disposal Certificates retained.

RIDDOR 2013 reportable incidents and accidents must be reported to the Authorised Officer and (where applicable) the HSE without delay; copies of any HSE Improvement or Prohibition Notices must be forwarded.

Portable electrical equipment must be ≤110 V and double insulated or effectively earthed, complying with the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 and the Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998.

Contractor is responsible for making good all damage caused during works at own expense, including protection of floors, fixtures, fittings, carpets and furniture, and full clean-up / waste removal on completion.
Confidentiality: all client information must be treated in the strictest confidence; the Contractor must comply with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and UK data-protection law.

Warranty: any equipment defect or breakdown occurring within twelve months of repair or installation must be rectified by the Contractor at no extra cost other than spare parts; faulty workmanship must be re-done within 14 days of notification.

Additional Work Reports: where extra work beyond the approved grant documentation is required to make equipment safe and operational, a report and estimate must be sent to the Grants Team and work must not commence until the Authorised Officer approves it.

Performance review meetings at a frequency set by the Authorised Officer will review customer satisfaction, response-time achievement, financial monitoring, invoice queries, abortive calls, quality of work, H&S compliance (including HSE inspections and RIDDOR incidents), DBS declarations and random audit inspections.

Pricing must be fully inclusive of all work required to complete the specified adaptation, including call-out, site clearance and waste disposal; the use of second-hand materials or equipment is not permitted.
All materials and workmanship must be of a quality acceptable to Bexley Council and compliant with the appropriate British Standards or their European equivalents.

warnings.message: Source was a .doc converted via Docling. Docling produced no stable page boundaries for this conversion (page_count=0). Evidence anchors therefore use section/code references (e.g., '#code/5.7.1') and a generic page_ref 'pg-1'; the document footer marks 'Page 23 of 23' but intermediate pages are not identifiable from the markdown.

Document states two different contract end dates. Header reads '1 November 2026 – 31 October 2030' while body 'PERIOD OF CONTRACT' clause states '1 November 2026 to 31 October 2028' with up to two one-year extensions (which would reach 2030). The 2028 base term with extensions is adopted as the primary requirement text; the 2030 header is treated as the full potential extended duration. Verify against executed Contract Terms and Conditions.
